sin(theta)cos(theta)>0 puts theta in quadrant I or III. The sum sin(theta)+cos(theta) is negative only in quadrant III. Of the choices, 6pi/5 lies in quadrant III.
The perimeter condition gives r(theta+2)=12. The area is A=(1/2)r^2 theta=72theta/(theta+2)^2, which is maximized for theta=2 (differentiate, or use symmetry of theta and 2).
For n/3 to be a square, exponent a of 2 is even and b-1 is even, so b is odd. For n/2 to be a fifth power, a-1 and b are multiples of 5. The least compatible exponents are a=6 and b=5; a+b=11.

Let t=log_2 x and A=log_2 a. The expression is (t-A)(2t-A)+2=2t^2-3At+A^2+2. Nonnegativity for all real t requires its discriminant 9A^2-8(A^2+2)=A^2-16<=0, so |A|<=4. The least a is 2^-4=1/16.
For P=(x,sqrt(x)), tan(theta)=1/sqrt(x), so sin^2(theta)=1/(x+1) and cos^2(theta)=x/(x+1). The condition gives (3x-1)/(x+1)=2, hence x=3 and the y-coordinate is sqrt(3).

The expression equals log_10(a+1)+log_10(b+1)=log_10((a+1)(b+1)). It is a natural number exactly when the product is 10, 100, or 1000, as 2<=a+1,b+1<=51. These give respectively 2, 7, and 4 ordered factor pairs, for a total of 13.

Put u=3^t>0. The vertical difference is D=3u^2-u+3^-k. For exactly two t-values with |D|=7/27, the level D=7/27 must have two positive roots; this requires 3^-k>7/27, so the natural k is 1. The roots have product (3^-1-7/27)/3=2/81, so p=log_3(2/81). Then (1/3)^p=3^-p=81/2 and k+3^-p=83/2.
